<reason>Side A won a close comparative debate by keeping the live question on gallons, not revenue. A conceded that steep tiers can cut outdoor use, then showed why that still does not make prices the controlling shortage tool: paying is compliance, so a tariff can miss a drought target even when everyone follows the rules. B’s fairness story was also damaged when B admitted a pool-and-lawn ban often asks nothing of the careful apartment. B remained vivid on fading enforcement in recurring drought, but “set the first jump high enough” restated the desired result rather than neutralizing A’s water-budget burden.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2: tariffs can miss the water target even with perfect compliance because paying is allowed, while a remaining paid gallon is an exemption rather than a stopped withdrawal.</best_rebuttal>
